newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 19.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 19. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesian President Suharto has said the government will not arbitrarily revoke publishing licences of the media but reminded the press to act responsibly.

The World Bank has said significant risks loom over Indonesia's economy despite its strong fundamentals because the current account deficit may worsen, deregulation has lost momentum and core inflation is still high.
The government has approved 1.3 rupiah trillion in domestic investment for the development of palm oil plantations, to be mostly located in Sumatra.
All the provincial branches of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), except for the branch in West Sumatra, have accepted the results of the May 29 general elections.
